seo_title: Cost of Living in Dubrovnik 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Dubrovnik per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A Schengen city on the Adriatic with a 1-year digital nomad visa and access to the entire EU. It combines medieval tourism and calm remote work by the sea.
pros: A Schengen country with a 1-year digital nomad visa
The sea and Adriatic infrastructure year-round
Low taxes for DNV residents (income tax exemption)
Close to Italy, Bosnia, Montenegro and Albania
UNESCO heritage and a relaxed pace
cons: A small job market — almost everyone works remotely

best_places.name: Stari Grad
best_places.description: A UNESCO site within the fortress walls — narrow streets, marble pavements and countless churches.

best_places.name: Lapad
best_places.description: A resort peninsula with beaches, villas and a quieter life year-round.

best_places.name: Saltwater Workspace
best_places.description: The main digital nomad coworking in Lapad, with meeting rooms and an event venue.

best_places.name: Lokrum Island
best_places.description: A nature reserve 15 minutes by boat: olive groves, peacocks and hidden coves.

visa_steps.title: Digital Nomad Visa
visa_steps.description: A Croatian visa for remote workers with an income from 2,870 euros a month. Residency for 1 year without extension.

visa_steps.title: Residence permit through work
visa_steps.description: A contract with a local employer — the standard route, but Dubrovnik's job market is small.

visa_steps.title: OIB (tax ID)
visa_steps.description: An identification number for a bank account, lease and company registration. Issued at the Porezna uprava.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: OTP, Erste, PBZ open accounts with a residence permit. Visa and MasterCard work all along the Adriatic.

visa_steps.title: Address registration
visa_steps.description: MUP — police registration of your place of residence. Without it you can't arrange health insurance.

faq.question: Can I stay in Dubrovnik without a visa?
faq.answer: No, you need a Schengen visa or a residence permit through the DNV.

faq.question: Which language is spoken in Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: Croatian, with English in tourism and IT. Russian is found among the older generation.

faq.question: What is winter like in Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: Tourists leave, there are fewer restaurants, but the climate stays +10–15°C. The city becomes quiet and local.

faq.question: What are the downsides of the DNV in Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: The visa can't be extended — after a year you either change your status or leave for six months.

faq.question: How is healthcare in Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: State HZZO is available with a residence permit. Private clinics are in Split; for complex cases people fly to Zagreb or Italy.

faq.question: Is it worth relocating with children to Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: There are international schools in Split (1.5 hours away). In Dubrovnik itself — only Croatian ones.

reviews.text: I got a one-year DNV: I work remotely from an apartment in Lapad. The sea outside the window, islands on weekends. But in a year I'll have to decide what's next — the visa can't be extended.
I lived here for half a year over summer — there were lots of tourists. In winter it got calmer. Dubrovnik is beautiful, but it's not for long-term settled living.
